subproblem.title: Restriction theory of currents of locally finite mass (Simon 2.7–2.9)
subproblem.statement: Let U ⊆ ℝ^P be open and k ∈ ℕ. (R0) If X ∈ D_k(U) has a measure representation (μ,v) (IsMeasureRepresentation), then M_W(X) < ∞ for every W ⊂⊂ U. (R1) Any two restrictions (IsRestriction) of X ∈ D_k(U) to the same set A are equal. (R2) If M_W(X) < ∞ for every W ⊂⊂ U, then there is a measure μ with IsMassMeasure X μ such that X has a restriction to every Borel set A, and every restriction S of X to a set A satisfies M_W(S) = μ(W ∩ A) for every open W ⊆ U.
subproblem.lean_statement: (∀ (P k : ℕ) (U : Set (Eucl P)), IsOpen U → ∀ (X : GeometricCurrentOn U k) (μ : Measure (Eucl P)) (v : Eucl P → NVector (Eucl P) k), IsMeasureRepresentation X μ v → ∀ W, CompactlyContainedOpen W U → X.massOn W < ∞) ∧ (∀ (P k : ℕ) (U : Set (Eucl P)), IsOpen U → ∀ (X : GeometricCurrentOn U k) (A : Set (Eucl P)) (S₁ S₂ : GeometricCurrentOn U k), IsRestriction X A S₁ → IsRestriction X A S₂ → S₁ = S₂) ∧ (∀ (P k : ℕ) (U : Set (Eucl P)), IsOpen U → ∀ X : GeometricCurrentOn U k, (∀ W, CompactlyContainedOpen W U → X.massOn W < ∞) → ∃ μ : Measure (Eucl P), IsMassMeasure X μ ∧ (∀ A : Set (Eucl P), MeasurableSet A → ∃ S : GeometricCurrentOn U k, IsRestriction X A S) ∧ ∀ (A : Set (Eucl P)) (S : GeometricCurrentOn U k), IsRestriction X A S → ∀ W : Set (Eucl P), IsOpen W → W ⊆ U → S.massOn W = μ (W ∩ A))
subproblem.natural_proof:
Conventions (fixed for this proof). ℝ^P := Eucl P with standard orthonormal basis e_1,…,e_P. Hᵏ := μHE[k], the normalized k-dimensional Hausdorff measure (a positive constant multiple of μH[k]; it equals Lebesgue measure on a k-dimensional Euclidean space, and μHE[0] = μH[0] is the counting measure). D_k(U) := GeometricCurrentOn U k; D^k(U) := TestFormOn U k (C^∞ k-forms on ℝ^P with compact tsupport contained in U). I(k,P) := the strictly increasing maps {1,…,k} → {1,…,P}; for I ∈ I(k,P), e_I := (e_{I(1)},…,e_{I(k)}) and dx^I is the constant k-covector with dx^I(e_J) = δ_{IJ} (J ∈ I(k,P)); every k-covector is α = Σ_I α(e_I) dx^I. |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α = (Σ_I α(e_I)²)^{1/2} (the norm used in the definition of mass), and ‖ω‖ := sup_x |ω(x)| for a form ω. For a k-vector w (an element of NVector = the dual of the k-covectors) put w^I := w(dx^I) and |w|_* := (Σ_I (w^I)²)^{1/2}; then w(α) = Σ_I α(e_I) w^I, so |w(α)| ≤ |α| |w|_* (Cauchy–Schwarz). M_W(X) := X.massOn W, M(X) := X.mass = M_U(X), spt X := X.support, X_j ⇀ X := WeaklyConvergesOn, ∂ := boundary. τ(M,θ,ξ)(ω) := tauAction = ∫_M θ ⟨ω,ξ⟩ dHᵏ with ⟨ω,ξ⟩(x) := ξ(x)(ω(x)); "i.m." := IsIntegerMultiplicity; "X⌞A" denotes a current S with IsRestriction X A S; W ⊂⊂ U := CompactlyContainedOpen W U. B_r(x), B̄_r(x) denote open and closed balls.

Source: (P1) of the parent proof, i.e. Simon Ch. 6, 2.7–2.9 (representation of currents of locally finite mass by the Riesz Representation Theorem, Ch. 1, 4.14; the characterization 2.8 of μ_T; the restriction 2.9), together with the independence of the restriction from the chosen representation that the contract's IsRestriction (2.9) refers to ("the result does not depend on the representation (uniqueness of the vector measure T⃗ μ_T)").

Fact used. (F1) If tsupport ω ⊆ W then |X(ω)| ≤ ‖ω‖ M_W(X): if ‖ω‖ = 0 then ω = 0; otherwise ±ω/‖ω‖ is admissible in the definition of M_W(X).

Part (R0): a measure representation forces locally finite mass.
1. Let (μ,v) be a measure representation of X ∈ D_k(U) (IsMeasureRepresentation: for every ω ∈ D^k(U), x ↦ v(x)(ω(x)) is μ-integrable and X(ω) = ∫ v(x)(ω(x)) dμ), and let W ⊂⊂ U. Choose φ ∈ C_c^∞(U) with 0 ≤ φ ≤ 1 and φ = 1 on the compact set closure(W) ⊆ U. For each I ∈ I(k,P), φ·dx^I ∈ D^k(U), so x ↦ φ(x) v^I(x) is μ-integrable and c_I := ∫_{closure W} |v^I| dμ < ∞.
2. If ω is admissible for M_W (tsupport ω ⊆ W, |ω| ≤ 1), then |v(x)(ω(x))| ≤ |ω(x)| |v(x)|_* ≤ Σ_I |v^I(x)| 1_{closure W}(x), so X(ω) ≤ Σ_I c_I. Hence M_W(X) ≤ Σ_I c_I < ∞.

Part (R1): restrictions are unique.
3. Let S_1, S_2 be restrictions of X to A, via representations (μ_1,v_1), (μ_2,v_2) of X (so A is measurable and S_l(ω) = ∫_A v_l(ω) dμ_l). As in step 1, ∫_K |v_l^I| dμ_l < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U and every I. Hence ν_l^I(B) := ∫_B v_l^I dμ_l (Borel B ⊆ U) defines signed Borel measures on U of locally finite total variation.
4. For φ ∈ C_c^∞(U): ∫ φ dν_1^I = X(φ dx^I) = ∫ φ dν_2^I. Every φ ∈ C_c(U) is the uniform limit of mollifications φ_ε ∈ C_c^∞(U) supported in a fixed compact subset K of U; by dominated convergence (|v_l^I| is μ_l-integrable on K) the identity extends to all φ ∈ C_c(U).
5. Hence ν_1^I = ν_2^I on Borel subsets of U: the positive locally finite Borel measures λ_1 := (ν_1^I)⁺ + (ν_2^I)⁻ and λ_2 := (ν_2^I)⁺ + (ν_1^I)⁻ on U (Jordan decompositions) have equal integrals against every φ ∈ C_c(U); locally finite Borel measures on the open set U ⊆ ℝ^P (a locally compact, σ-compact metric space) are regular and are determined by these integrals (Riesz uniqueness, Simon Ch. 1, 4.12; Mathlib `Measure.ext_of_integral_eq_on_compactlySupported`). So λ_1 = λ_2.
6. Let ω ∈ D^k(U); write ω = Σ_I ω_I dx^I with ω_I := ω(·)(e_I) ∈ C_c^∞(U), so v_l(x)(ω(x)) = Σ_I ω_I(x) v_l^I(x), and ω vanishes off the compact K := tsupport ω ⊆ U. Then S_l(ω) = Σ_I ∫_{A∩K} ω_I dν_l^I, which by step 5 is the same for l = 1, 2. Thus S_1(ω) = S_2(ω) for all ω, and S_1 = S_2 (GeometricCurrentOn.ext).

Part (R2): mass measure, existence of restrictions, mass identity. Assume M_W(X) < ∞ for all W ⊂⊂ U. Let N := #I(k,P) and identify a k-covector α with its coefficient vector (α(e_I))_I ∈ ℝ^N; this is an isometry between |·| and the Euclidean norm of ℝ^N.
7. (Extension to continuous forms.) Let K_c(U;ℝ^N) be the continuous maps φ : U → ℝ^N with compact support in U. For such φ choose W ⊂⊂ U with spt φ ⊆ W; componentwise mollification gives test forms ω_ε with tsupport ω_ε ⊆ W for small ε, ‖ω_ε − φ‖ → 0 and |ω_ε| ≤ sup|φ| pointwise (mollification is an average and the Euclidean ball is convex). By (F1), |X(ω_ε) − X(ω_δ)| ≤ M_W(X)‖ω_ε − ω_δ‖ → 0, so L(φ) := lim_ε X(ω_ε) exists, does not depend on the approximating sequence, is linear, equals X on test forms, and |L(φ)| ≤ M_W(X) sup|φ| whenever spt φ ⊆ W ⊂⊂ U. Moreover, for every open W′ ⊆ U,
   sup{L(φ) : φ ∈ K_c(U;ℝ^N), spt φ ⊆ W′, |φ| ≤ 1} = M_{W′}(X):
   "≥" since admissible test forms are such φ; "≤" since for spt φ compact ⊆ W′ the mollifications are admissible for M_{W′} when ε is small, and L(φ) = lim X(ω_ε).
8. (Riesz.) L is a locally bounded linear functional on K_c(U;ℝ^N). By the Riesz Representation Theorem (Simon Ch. 1, 4.14; SimonGMT `simon_theorem_4_14`, on the locally compact Hausdorff space U with the finite-dimensional Hilbert space ℝ^N) there are a Radon measure μ_0 on U and a μ_0-measurable ν : U → ℝ^N with |ν| = 1 μ_0-a.e. and L(φ) = ∫ ⟨φ, ν⟩ dμ_0; moreover μ_0 is the total variation measure of L: by (∗) in the proof of 4.14 (the envelope identity sup{L(φ) : |φ| ≤ g} = ∫ g dμ_0 for g ∈ C_c(U), g ≥ 0; SimonGMT `vectorFunctionalEnvelopeMeasure`) and inner regularity of μ_0 on open sets, μ_0(W′) = sup{L(φ) : spt φ ⊆ W′, |φ| ≤ 1} for every open W′ ⊆ U. By step 7, μ_0(W′) = M_{W′}(X) for every open W′ ⊆ U. Define the Borel measure μ on ℝ^P by μ(B) := μ_0(B ∩ U), and replace ν by a Borel function equal to it μ_0-a.e. Then μ(ℝ^P ∖ U) = 0 and μ(W) = M_W(X) for every W ⊂⊂ U, i.e. IsMassMeasure X μ.
9. (Representation.) Let v(x) be the k-vector with coefficients v^I(x) := ν_I(x) for x ∈ U (v := 0 off U), i.e. v(x)(α) := Σ_I α(e_I) ν_I(x). For ω ∈ D^k(U): |v(x)(ω(x))| ≤ |ω(x)| |ν(x)| ≤ ‖ω‖ 1_{tsupport ω}(x) μ-a.e., which is μ-integrable since tsupport ω is a compact subset of U and μ is finite on it; and X(ω) = L(ω) = ∫ v(x)(ω(x)) dμ. So (μ, v) is a measure representation of X, with |v|_* = 1 μ-a.e.
10. (Existence of restrictions.) For a Borel set A ⊆ ℝ^P put S_A(ω) := ∫_A v(x)(ω(x)) dμ. S_A is linear on D^k(U); it is sequentially continuous: if ω_j → 0 in the test-form topology (tsupport ω_j ⊆ K for a fixed compact K ⊆ U and ω_j → 0 uniformly), then |S_A(ω_j)| ≤ ‖ω_j‖ μ(K) → 0. Thus S_A ∈ D_k(U) and IsRestriction X A S_A holds via the representation (μ, v).
11. (Mass identity.) Let S be any restriction of X to a set A (so A is measurable) and W ⊆ U open. By (R1), S = S_A.
   "≤": for admissible ω (tsupport ω ⊆ W, |ω| ≤ 1), S_A(ω) ≤ ∫_{A∩W} |ω||v|_* dμ ≤ μ(W ∩ A).
   "≥": let K ⊆ A ∩ W be compact and ε > 0. By Lusin's theorem (μ_0 Radon, ν measurable) there is a compact K′ ⊆ K with μ(K ∖ K′) < ε such that ν|_{K′} is continuous and |ν| = 1 on K′; by outer regularity there is an open O with K′ ⊆ O, closure(O) compact ⊆ W, μ(O ∖ K′) < ε. Extend ν|_{K′} (Tietze, componentwise), compose with the radial retraction of ℝ^N onto its closed unit ball and multiply by a cutoff in C_c(O) equal to 1 on K′: this gives φ ∈ K_c(U;ℝ^N) with spt φ ⊆ O, |φ| ≤ 1, φ = ν on K′. Then ∫_A ⟨φ,ν⟩ dμ ≥ μ(K′) − μ(O ∖ K′) ≥ μ(K) − 2ε. The mollifications ω_ε of φ are admissible for M_W for small ε and converge to φ uniformly with supports in closure(O), so S_A(ω_ε) → ∫_A ⟨φ,ν⟩ dμ (dominated convergence). Hence M_W(S) ≥ μ(K) − 2ε. By inner regularity of the Radon measure μ_0 on the Borel set A ∩ W ⊆ U (valid also when μ(A ∩ W) = ∞, U being σ-compact), the supremum of μ(K) over compact K ⊆ A ∩ W is μ(W ∩ A). So M_W(S) = μ(W ∩ A).
12. Steps 8, 10, 11 give (R2). Together with (R0) and (R1) this proves the three conjuncts. ∎
proof_key_steps: (R0): testing with φ dx^I (φ = 1 near closure W) bounds M_W(X) by Σ_I ∫_{closure W}|v^I| dμ.
(R1): the coefficient signed measures of two representations agree on C_c^∞(U), hence on C_c(U), hence as measures (Riesz uniqueness), so the restrictions agree.
(R2): by the mass bound X extends to continuous compactly supported forms; the Riesz Representation Theorem (Ch. 1, 4.14) gives μ and ν with |ν| = 1 and μ(W′) = M_{W′}(X).
S_A(ω) := ∫_A⟨ω,v⟩dμ is a current and a restriction of X to A.
Mass identity M_W(S) = μ(W ∩ A): '≤' from |v|_* = 1, '≥' by Lusin approximation, mollification and inner regularity.

audit.reason: All three conjuncts match the prose. Coordinate cutoff estimates establish local finite mass; local measure uniqueness proves restriction uniqueness; Riesz representation and approximation establish existence and the mass identity for every open W ⊆ U.

subproblem.title: Smooth push-forward of integer multiplicity currents (P3)
subproblem.statement: Assume LipschitzPushforwardIntegerMultiplicity (Simon 3.9). Let U ⊆ ℝ^P, V ⊆ ℝ^Q be open, X ∈ D_{k+1}(U) integer multiplicity, and f : ℝ^P → ℝ^Q of class C^∞ with f(U) ⊆ V and f⁻¹(K) ∩ spt X compact for every compact K ⊆ V. Then there is an integer multiplicity S ∈ D_{k+1}(V) (the push-forward f_#X) such that: (1) S(ω) = X(η) whenever η ∈ D^{k+1}(U) agrees with the pull-back f^#ω on an open set containing spt X; (2) ∂S(ω) = ∂X(η) whenever ω ∈ D^k(V) and η ∈ D^k(U) agrees with f^#ω on an open set containing spt X; (3) if c ≥ 0 and ‖Df(x)‖ ≤ c for all x, then M_W(S) ≤ c^{k+1} M_{f⁻¹(W)∩U}(X) and M_W(∂S) ≤ c^k M_{f⁻¹(W)∩U}(∂X) for every W ⊆ ℝ^Q.

Source: (P3) of the parent proof (Simon Ch. 6, 2.23–2.24 for smooth maps, and 3.9 via the sibling `LipschitzPushforwardIntegerMultiplicity`), including its detailed identification of the Lipschitz push-forward with the classical smooth push-forward f_#X(ω) = X(ζ f^#ω); copied and filled in. Degree n := k + 1 ≥ 1.

Notation and facts.
- For a linear L : ℝ^P → ℝ^Q and a j-covector α on ℝ^Q, L^#α := α∘(L,…,L) (`ContinuousAlternatingMap.compContinuousLinearMap α L`); (f^#ω)(x) := Df(x)^# ω(f(x)) with Df(x) := fderiv ℝ f x.
(F1) |Y(ω)| ≤ ‖ω‖ M_W(Y) if tsupport ω ⊆ W.
(F2) (Support.) If η, η′ ∈ D^j(U) agree on an open set N ⊇ spt Y (Y ∈ D_j(U)), then Y(η) = Y(η′): K := tsupport(η − η′) ⊆ ℝ^P ∖ N is a compact subset of U ∖ spt Y, which is the union of the open sets W (closure W compact ⊆ U) on which Y vanishes; finitely many such W_1,…,W_l cover K, and with a smooth partition of unity χ_i ∈ C_c^∞(W_i), Σχ_i = 1 near K, Y(η − η′) = Σ_i Y(χ_i(η − η′)) = 0.
(F3) (Pull-back norm.) |L^#α| ≤ ‖L‖^j |α| for j-covectors α. [In the Euclidean structures on j-covectors for which {dx^I} are orthonormal, L^# is the j-th exterior power of the adjoint of L; by the singular value decomposition L = Σ_i σ_i u_i⊗v_i (orthonormal u, v), Λ^j is diagonal in the bases {v_I}, {u_I} with entries ∏_{i∈I}σ_i ≤ ‖L‖^j.]
(F4) (Naturality.) For C^∞ f and a smooth j-form ω on ℝ^Q, d(f^#ω) = f^#(dω) (chain rule and symmetry of second derivatives; standard).
(F5) (Compatible test forms exist.) For ω ∈ D^j(V), K_ω := spt X ∩ f⁻¹(tsupport ω) is compact (properness hypothesis); take ζ ∈ C_c^∞(U), 0 ≤ ζ ≤ 1, ζ = 1 on an open O ⊇ K_ω; then η := ζ·f^#ω ∈ D^j(U) and η = f^#ω on the open set N := O ∪ f⁻¹(ℝ^Q ∖ tsupport ω) ⊇ spt X, with tsupport η ⊆ tsupport ζ ∩ f⁻¹(tsupport ω).

Proof.
1. (The sibling push-forward.) f is C^∞, hence locally Lipschitz on U; f maps U into V; X is i.m.; and f⁻¹(K) ∩ spt X is compact for compact K ⊆ V. By the hypothesis `LipschitzPushforwardIntegerMultiplicity` there is an i.m. S ∈ D_n(V) with IsLipschitzPushforward X f S: there are a rectifiable triple (M,θ,ξ) in U (θ > 0 real and integrable on compact subsets of U — not necessarily integer valued or ≥ 1) with X = τ(M,θ,ξ), and linear maps L(x) such that for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M, every weighted tangent space T of (M,θ) at x and every v ∈ T, the derivative of t ↦ f(x + tv) at 0 is L(x)v; and S(ω) = ∫_M θ ⟨ω(f(x)), L(x)_#ξ(x)⟩ dHⁿ for ω ∈ D^n(V) (L(x)_# = nVectorPushforward n (L x)).
2. (L(x) = Df(x) on the tangent plane.) For Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M the orients property gives an orthonormal τ spanning a weighted tangent space T_x with ξ(x) = ±simpleNVector τ. For v = τ_i ∈ T_x, t ↦ f(x + tv) has derivative Df(x)τ_i at 0 (f is differentiable), so L(x)τ_i = Df(x)τ_i by uniqueness of derivatives. Hence (`nVectorPushforward_simple`) L(x)_#ξ(x) = ±simpleNVector(L(x)∘τ) = ±simpleNVector(Df(x)∘τ) = Df(x)_#ξ(x), and by duality (nVectorPushforward is precomposition with the covector pull-back, (1.9)) ⟨ω(f(x)), Df(x)_#ξ(x)⟩ = ⟨(f^#ω)(x), ξ(x)⟩. Therefore
   S(ω) = ∫_M θ ⟨(f^#ω)(x), ξ(x)⟩ dHⁿ(x) for all ω ∈ D^n(V).
3. (Hⁿ(M ∖ spt X) = 0.) Let O′ := U ∖ spt X (open). By (F2) (with η′ = 0), X vanishes on every test form supported in O′. The coefficient measures θξ^I Hⁿ⌞M (locally finite total variation on U: |ξ^I| ≤ |ξ|_* = 1 a.e. since ξ = ±simpleNVector τ with τ orthonormal (Cauchy–Binet), and θ is integrable on compacts) thus annihilate every φ ∈ C_c^∞(O′) (test X with φ dx^I), hence every φ ∈ C_c(O′) (uniform approximation with supports in a fixed compact subset of O′, dominated convergence), hence they vanish on Borel subsets of O′ (Riesz uniqueness for locally finite signed measures on O′, via Jordan decompositions). So θξ = 0 Hⁿ-a.e. on M ∩ O′; since θ > 0 on M and |ξ|_* = 1 a.e. on M, Hⁿ(M ∩ O′) = 0.

subproblem.title: Locality of weighted approximate tangent spaces
subproblem.statement: For P, n ∈ ℕ, Hⁿ-null-measurable sets M, M′ ⊆ ℝ^P (Hⁿ = μHE[n]), functions θ, θ′ : ℝ^P → ℝ and a point x with θ(x) = θ′(x): if for some ρ > 0 the function θ is Hⁿ-integrable on M ∩ B̄_ρ(x) and θ′ on M′ ∩ B̄_ρ(x), and if r^{−n}∫_{B̄_{Rr}(x)} |1_Mθ − 1_{M′}θ′| dHⁿ → 0 as r ↓ 0 for every R > 0, then for every linear subspace Q of ℝ^P, Q is a weighted approximate tangent space of (M,θ) at x in the sense of Simon Ch. 3, 1.7 (HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt) if and only if it is one of (M′,θ′) at x.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (M M' : Set (Eucl P)) (θ θ' : Eucl P → ℝ) (x : Eucl P), NullMeasurableSet M (μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl P)) → NullMeasurableSet M' (μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl P)) → θ x = θ' x → (∃ ρ : ℝ, 0 < ρ ∧ IntegrableOn θ (M ∩ closedBall x ρ) (μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl P)) ∧ IntegrableOn θ' (M' ∩ closedBall x ρ) (μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl P))) → (∀ R : ℝ, 0 < R → Tendsto (fun r : ℝ => ENNReal.ofReal ((r ^ n)⁻¹) * ∫⁻ z in closedBall x (R * r), ‖M.indicator θ z - M'.indicator θ' z‖ₑ ∂(μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl P))) (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 0)) → ∀ Q : Submodule ℝ (Eucl P), HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M θ x Q ↔ HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M' θ' x Q
subproblem.natural_proof:
Conventions (fixed for this proof). ℝ^P := Eucl P with standard orthonormal basis e_1,…,e_P. Hᵏ := μHE[k], the normalized k-dimensional Hausdorff measure (a positive constant multiple of μH[k]; it equals Lebesgue measure on a k-dimensional Euclidean space, and μHE[0] = μH[0] is the counting measure). D_k(U) := GeometricCurrentOn U k; D^k(U) := TestFormOn U k (C^∞ k-forms on ℝ^P with compact tsupport contained in U). I(k,P) := the strictly increasing maps {1,…,k} → {1,…,P}; for I ∈ I(k,P), e_I := (e_{I(1)},…,e_{I(k)}) and dx^I is the constant k-covector with dx^I(e_J) = δ_{IJ} (J ∈ I(k,P)); every k-covector is α = Σ_I α(e_I) dx^I. |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α = (Σ_I α(e_I)²)^{1/2} (the norm used in the definition of mass), and ‖ω‖ := sup_x |ω(x)| for a form ω. For a k-vector w (an element of NVector = the dual of the k-covectors) put w^I := w(dx^I) and |w|_* := (Σ_I (w^I)²)^{1/2}; then w(α) = Σ_I α(e_I) w^I, so |w(α)| ≤ |α| |w|_* (Cauchy–Schwarz). M_W(X) := X.massOn W, M(X) := X.mass = M_U(X), spt X := X.support, X_j ⇀ X := WeaklyConvergesOn, ∂ := boundary. τ(M,θ,ξ)(ω) := tauAction = ∫_M θ ⟨ω,ξ⟩ dHᵏ with ⟨ω,ξ⟩(x) := ξ(x)(ω(x)); "i.m." := IsIntegerMultiplicity; "X⌞A" denotes a current S with IsRestriction X A S; W ⊂⊂ U := CompactlyContainedOpen W U. B_r(x), B̄_r(x) denote open and closed balls.

Source: this is the locality property of Simon's weighted approximate tangent spaces (Ch. 3, 1.7), used in the parent proof in (P4)(iv) ("the weighted approximate tangent space at x ∈ V_i depends only on M ∩ V_i and θ|V_i modulo Hᵏ-null sets (for small r the blow-up integrals only see x + r·spt f ⊆ V_i, and Hᵏ(η_{x,r}Z) = r^{−k}Hᵏ(Z) = 0 for null Z)") and in the same way in Steps 2, 11 and (P5). Here it is stated and proved in the quantitative form needed by all those uses.

Notation. Hⁿ := μHE[n] = c_n·μH[n] with a constant c_n ∈ (0,∞). η_{x,r}(y) := blowUpMap x r y = r⁻¹(y − x). Recall the definition: HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M θ x Q means dim Q = n and, for every f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P,ℝ), I_{M,θ}(r) := ∫_{η_{x,r}(M)} f(y) θ(x + r y) dHⁿ(y) → θ(x) ∫_Q f dHⁿ as r → 0, r > 0.

1. (Change of variables under the blow-up.) Fix r > 0. The map η_{x,r} is an affine bijection of ℝ^P (a translation followed by the dilation by r⁻¹) with inverse z ↦ x + r z, and for every set A ⊆ ℝ^P, Hⁿ(η_{x,r}(A)) = r^{−n} Hⁿ(A): Hausdorff measure is translation invariant and scales by λⁿ under the dilation y ↦ λy (Mathlib `hausdorffMeasure_smul`, `hausdorffMeasure_smul_right_image`; the constant c_n does not matter). Equivalently, the push-forward of Hⁿ⌞A under the measurable equivalence η_{x,r} is rⁿ·Hⁿ⌞η_{x,r}(A). Hence, for every g : ℝ^P → ℝ,
   ∫_{η_{x,r}(A)} g dHⁿ = r^{−n} ∫_A g(η_{x,r}(z)) dHⁿ(z),
   both sides being integrable or not simultaneously (change of variables under a measurable equivalence that multiplies the measure by a constant; with the Bochner convention both sides are 0 in the non-integrable case).
2. Applying step 1 with A = M and g(y) := f(y) θ(x + r y), and using x + r·η_{x,r}(z) = z, we get for every r > 0
   I_{M,θ}(r) = r^{−n} ∫_M f(η_{x,r}(z)) θ(z) dHⁿ(z) = r^{−n} ∫ f(η_{x,r}(z)) (1_M θ)(z) dHⁿ(z),
   and the same formula for (M′, θ′). The second equality (integral over M = integral of the indicator) uses that M is Hⁿ-null-measurable (Mathlib `integral_indicator₀`); this hypothesis is essential: for a non-measurable M (e.g. a Bernstein set) the restricted measure Hⁿ⌞M and the lower integral of 1_M can disagree, and the statement would fail.
3. The dimension conditions dim Q = n in the two definitions are identical, so it remains to compare the limits. Fix f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P,ℝ), choose R ≥ 1 with spt f ⊆ B̄_R(0), and let ‖f‖_∞ := sup|f|. Let ρ > 0 be as in the hypothesis. For 0 < r < ρ/R: f(η_{x,r}(z)) ≠ 0 implies |z − x| ≤ R r < ρ, so the integrand of step 2 vanishes outside B̄_ρ(x); on M ∩ B̄_ρ(x) it is the product of the bounded continuous function f∘η_{x,r} with θ, which is Hⁿ-integrable there by hypothesis. Since M is null-measurable, 1_Mθ is a.e.-strongly measurable on B̄_ρ(x) (`AEStronglyMeasurable.indicator₀`), so the integrand is integrable; likewise for (M′,θ′). In particular |1_Mθ − 1_{M′}θ′| is a.e.-measurable on B̄_ρ(x), so its lower integral below is a genuine integral.
4. Consequently, for 0 < r < ρ/R,
   |I_{M,θ}(r) − I_{M′,θ′}(r)| = r^{−n} |∫ f(η_{x,r}(z)) (1_Mθ − 1_{M′}θ′)(z) dHⁿ(z)| ≤ ‖f‖_∞ r^{−n} ∫_{B̄_{Rr}(x)} |1_Mθ − 1_{M′}θ′| dHⁿ,
   because |f∘η_{x,r}| ≤ ‖f‖_∞ · 1_{B̄_{Rr}(x)}. By hypothesis (applied with this R) the right side tends to 0 as r ↓ 0 (in ℝ≥0∞, hence eventually finite and then tending to 0 as real numbers). So I_{M,θ}(r) − I_{M′,θ′}(r) → 0 as r → 0⁺.
5. Since θ(x) = θ′(x), the two prescribed limits θ(x)∫_Q f dHⁿ and θ′(x)∫_Q f dHⁿ coincide. By step 4, I_{M,θ}(r) tends to this number if and only if I_{M′,θ′}(r) does. As f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P,ℝ) was arbitrary, HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M θ x Q holds if and only if HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M′ θ′ x Q holds, for every subspace Q. ∎
proof_key_steps: Change of variables under the blow-up η_{x,r}: ∫_{η_{x,r}(A)} g dHⁿ = r^{−n}∫_A g∘η_{x,r} dHⁿ (translation invariance and scaling of Hausdorff measure).
Using null-measurability of M, M′, the blow-up integrals equal r^{−n}∫ f((z−x)/r)(1_Mθ)(z) dHⁿ(z) and are integrable for r < ρ/R (spt f ⊆ B̄_R(0)).
Their difference is at most ‖f‖_∞ r^{−n}∫_{B̄_{Rr}(x)}|1_Mθ − 1_{M′}θ′| dHⁿ, which tends to 0.
θ(x) = θ′(x) makes the prescribed limits equal, and the dimension conditions coincide, so the two tangent-space conditions are equivalent.

(b) Every restriction of an integer multiplicity X ∈ D_k(U) to a set A is integer multiplicity. (c) If X, Y ∈ D_k(U) are integer multiplicity, a, b ∈ ℤ and Z(ω) = aX(ω) + bY(ω) for all test forms ω, then Z is integer multiplicity.

Written out for the contract's definitions (weighted approximate tangent spaces, Ch. 3, 1.7).

Preliminaries on a rectifiable triple (M,θ,ξ) (IsRectifiableTriple U k M θ ξ).
(i) |ξ(x)|_* = 1 for Hᵏ-a.e. x ∈ M: a.e. ξ(x) = ±simpleNVector τ with τ orthonormal, its coefficients are the minors det(τ_I), and Σ_I det(τ_I)² = det(τᵀτ) = 1 (Cauchy–Binet).
(ii) (Hᵏ⌞M, θξ) is a measure representation of τ(M,θ,ξ): for ω ∈ D^k(U), |θ ξ(ω)| ≤ ‖ω‖ θ 1_{tsupport ω} a.e. on M, which is integrable (θ is integrable on M ∩ tsupport ω, a compact subset of U), measurability coming from that of θ, ξ, ω; and τ(M,θ,ξ)(ω) = ∫ θ ξ(ω) d(Hᵏ⌞M).

If ν is a locally finite Borel measure on U and E ⊆ U is a Borel (or Hᵏ-null-measurable) set with ν(E) = 0, then Θ*ᵏ(ν, x) := limsup_{r↓0} ν(B̄_r(x))/(ω_k r^k) = 0 for Hᵏ-a.e. x ∈ E. [3.6 applied to ν⌞(U∖E) restricted to relatively compact open subsets of U.] In particular, if g ≥ 0 is locally Hᵏ-integrable on an Hᵏ-null-measurable set M′ ⊆ U and E ∩ M′ = ∅ (E null-measurable), then for every R > 0, r^{−k}∫_{B̄_{Rr}(x) ∩ M′} g dHᵏ → 0 for Hᵏ-a.e. x ∈ E.
(v) (Normalized Lebesgue points.) Let λ be a locally finite Borel measure on U, f ∈ L¹_loc(λ) (real or vector valued). For λ-a.e. x, λ(B̄_r(x))^{−1}∫_{B̄_r(x)} |f − f(x)| dλ → 0 (Lebesgue–Besicovitch differentiation theorem: Simon Ch. 1, 3.23 with the Symmetric Vitali Property 3.11(3); Mathlib `VitaliFamily.ae_tendsto_average_abs_sub` for the Besicovitch Vitali family). 1. S′(ω) := τ(M ∩ A, θ, ξ)(ω) = ∫_A θ ξ(ω) d(Hᵏ⌞M) defines a current: it is linear, and sequentially continuous by dominated convergence (if ω_j → 0 in D^k(U) with tsupport ω_j ⊆ K, then |θξ(ω_j)| ≤ ‖ω_j‖θ1_K). By (ii), IsRestriction X A S′ holds (via the representation (Hᵏ⌞M, θξ)). By `iwl_restriction_theory` ((R1), second conjunct), S = S′.

(M ∩ A, θ, ξ) is a rectifiable triple with θ ∈ {1,2,…} on M ∩ A: M ∩ A ⊆ U; it is null-measurable (M null-measurable, A measurable); countably k-rectifiable (a subset of M; `CountablyRectifiable.mono`); θ > 0 and integrable on M ∩ A ∩ K; ξ is AE-strongly measurable for Hᵏ⌞(M ∩ A) (restriction of Hᵏ⌞M). Orients: for Hᵏ-a.e. x ∈ M ∩ A, the orients property of (M,θ,ξ) holds at x with a frame τ, and by (iv) (with E := M ∩ A, M′ := M ∖ A, g := θ, using (iii)) r^{−k}∫_{B̄_{Rr}(x)} |1_Mθ − 1_{M∩A}θ| dHᵏ = r^{−k}∫_{B̄_{Rr}(x) ∩ (M∖A)} θ dHᵏ → 0 for every R > 0. By `iwl_weighted_tangent_locality` (M and M ∩ A are Hᵏ-null-measurable; same value θ(x); θ integrable on M ∩ B̄_ρ(x) for B̄_ρ(x) ⊆ U), HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt k (M∩A) θ x (span τ) holds, and ξ(x) = ±simpleNVector τ.
3. Hence S = τ(M ∩ A, θ, ξ) is integer multiplicity.

subproblem.title: Patching lemma: integer multiplicity is a local property
subproblem.statement: Let U ⊆ ℝ^P be open, k ∈ ℕ and X ∈ D_k(U). If every x ∈ U has an open neighbourhood V ⊆ U and an integer multiplicity Y ∈ D_k(U) such that X(ω) = Y(ω) for every test form ω with tsupport ω ⊆ V, then X is integer multiplicity.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P k : ℕ) (U : Set (Eucl P)), IsOpen U → ∀ X : GeometricCurrentOn U k, (∀ x ∈ U, ∃ V : Set (Eucl P), IsOpen V ∧ x ∈ V ∧ V ⊆ U ∧ ∃ Y : GeometricCurrentOn U k, IsIntegerMultiplicity Y ∧ ∀ ω : TestFormOn U k, tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) k) ⊆ V → X ω = Y ω) → IsIntegerMultiplicity X
subproblem.natural_proof:
Conventions (fixed for this proof). ℝ^P := Eucl P with standard orthonormal basis e_1,…,e_P. Hᵏ := μHE[k], the normalized k-dimensional Hausdorff measure (a positive constant multiple of μH[k]; it equals Lebesgue measure on a k-dimensional Euclidean space, and μHE[0] = μH[0] is the counting measure). D_k(U) := GeometricCurrentOn U k; D^k(U) := TestFormOn U k (C^∞ k-forms on ℝ^P with compact tsupport contained in U). I(k,P) := the strictly increasing maps {1,…,k} → {1,…,P}; for I ∈ I(k,P), e_I := (e_{I(1)},…,e_{I(k)}) and dx^I is the constant k-covector with dx^I(e_J) = δ_{IJ} (J ∈ I(k,P)); every k-covector is α = Σ_I α(e_I) dx^I. |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α = (Σ_I α(e_I)²)^{1/2} (the norm used in the definition of mass), and ‖ω‖ := sup_x |ω(x)| for a form ω. For a k-vector w (an element of NVector = the dual of the k-covectors) put w^I := w(dx^I) and |w|_* := (Σ_I (w^I)²)^{1/2}; then w(α) = Σ_I α(e_I) w^I, so |w(α)| ≤ |α| |w|_* (Cauchy–Schwarz). M_W(X) := X.massOn W, M(X) := X.mass = M_U(X), spt X := X.support, X_j ⇀ X := WeaklyConvergesOn, ∂ := boundary. τ(M,θ,ξ)(ω) := tauAction = ∫_M θ ⟨ω,ξ⟩ dHᵏ with ⟨ω,ξ⟩(x) := ξ(x)(ω(x)); "i.m." := IsIntegerMultiplicity; "X⌞A" denotes a current S with IsRestriction X A S; W ⊂⊂ U := CompactlyContainedOpen W U. B_r(x), B̄_r(x) denote open and closed balls.

(a) For a rectifiable triple (M,θ,ξ) (IsRectifiableTriple U k M θ ξ): |ξ(x)|_* = 1 for Hᵏ-a.e. x ∈ M. Indeed, a.e. ξ(x) = ±simpleNVector τ with τ orthonormal, whose coefficients are (simpleNVector τ)^I = dx^I(τ_1,…,τ_k) = det(τ_I) (the k×k minor of the P×k matrix of τ with rows I), and Σ_I det(τ_I)² = det(τᵀτ) = 1 by the Cauchy–Binet formula.
(b) For such a triple, the coefficient measures ν^I := θ ξ^I Hᵏ⌞M (I ∈ I(k,P)) are signed Borel measures on U of locally finite total variation (θ is integrable on M ∩ K for compact K ⊆ U and |ξ^I| ≤ |ξ|_* = 1 a.e. on M), and for every test form ω = Σ_I ω_I dx^I (ω_I := ω(·)(e_I) ∈ C_c^∞(U)) we have τ(M,θ,ξ)(ω) = Σ_I ∫ ω_I dν^I.
(c) (Uniqueness of vector measures.) Let O ⊆ U be open and ν, ν′ be ℝ^{I(k,P)}-valued Borel measures on O whose coefficients have locally finite total variation. If Σ_I ∫ω_I dν^I = Σ_I ∫ω_I dν′^I for all smooth k-forms ω with compact tsupport in O, then ν = ν′ on Borel subsets of O. Proof: testing with ω = φ dx^I (φ ∈ C_c^∞(O)) gives ∫φ dν^I = ∫φ dν′^I; every φ ∈ C_c(O) is a uniform limit of mollifications φ_ε ∈ C_c^∞(O) with supports in a fixed compact subset of O, so by dominated convergence the identity holds for φ ∈ C_c(O); then the positive locally finite Borel measures (ν^I)⁺ + (ν′^I)⁻ and (ν′^I)⁺ + (ν^I)⁻ on O have the same integrals against C_c(O), hence coincide (Riesz uniqueness for locally finite Borel measures on the locally compact σ-compact metric space O; Simon Ch. 1, 4.12/4.14; Mathlib `Measure.ext_of_integral_eq_on_compactlySupported`), i.e. ν^I = ν′^I.
(d) (Total variation.) If ν = gξλ with λ a positive measure, g ≥ 0 locally λ-integrable and |ξ|_* = 1 λ-a.e., then the total variation measure of ν with respect to |·|_* is gλ (|ν|(B) = ∫_B g|ξ|_* dλ).

2. (Compatibility.) Fix i, i′ and O := V_i ∩ V_{i′}. For every test form ω with tsupport ω ⊆ O we have Y_i(ω) = X(ω) = Y_{i′}(ω). Since θ_i > 0 on M_i and θ_{i′} > 0 on M_{i′}: Hᵏ((M_i Δ M_{i′}) ∩ O) = 0 and θ_i = θ_{i′} Hᵏ-a.e. on M_i ∩ M_{i′} ∩ O. In the same way the coefficient densities 1_{M_i}θ_iξ_i^I and 1_{M_{i′}}θ_{i′}ξ_{i′}^I agree λ-a.e., hence ξ_i = ξ_{i′} Hᵏ-a.e. on M_i ∩ M_{i′} ∩ O.
3. (Construction.) Let D_i := V_i ∖ ⋃_{j<i} V_j: pairwise disjoint Borel sets with ⋃_i D_i = U and D_i ⊆ V_i. Put M := ⋃_i (M_i ∩ D_i), and for x ∈ D_i set θ(x) := θ_i(x), ξ(x) := ξ_i(x); outside U put θ := 1, ξ := 0. Then for x ∈ M ∩ D_i we have x ∈ M_i and θ(x) = θ_i(x) ∈ {1,2,…}.
4. (Local agreement.) For each i: Hᵏ((M Δ M_i) ∩ V_i) = 0, and 1_Mθ = 1_{M_i}θ_i, 1_Mθξ = 1_{M_i}θ_iξ_i Hᵏ-a.e. on V_i. Indeed V_i = ⋃_j (V_i ∩ D_j), on V_i ∩ D_j the triple (M,θ,ξ) equals (M_j,θ_j,ξ_j), and by step 2 (with O = V_i ∩ V_j ⊇ V_i ∩ D_j) the latter agrees Hᵏ-a.e. with (M_i,θ_i,ξ_i) there.
5. (Representation.) Let ω ∈ D^k(U). Its tsupport is a compact subset of U, covered by finitely many V_i, say V_1,…,V_l after relabeling; choose a smooth partition of unity χ_1,…,χ_l with χ_i ∈ C_c^∞(V_i) and Σ_iχ_i = 1 on a neighbourhood of tsupport ω. Then ω = Σ_i χ_iω, tsupport(χ_iω) ⊆ V_i, so
   X(ω) = Σ_i X(χ_iω) = Σ_i Y_i(χ_iω) = Σ_i ∫_{M_i} θ_i χ_i ⟨ω,ξ_i⟩ dHᵏ = Σ_i ∫_M θ χ_i ⟨ω,ξ⟩ dHᵏ = ∫_M θ ⟨ω,ξ⟩ dHᵏ,
   using step 4 on V_i ⊇ spt χ_i in the fourth equality (all integrands are integrable by step 6 below). Hence X(ω) = τ(M,θ,ξ)(ω) for every ω ∈ D^k(U).
6. (IsRectifiableTriple U k M θ ξ.)
   - M ⊆ ⋃_i D_i = U.
   - M is Hᵏ-null-measurable: a countable union of the null-measurable sets M_i intersected with Borel sets D_i.
   - M is countably k-rectifiable: M ⊆ ⋃_i M_i and each M_i ⊆ M_{i,0} ∪ ⋃_j F_{i,j}(ℝᵏ) with Hᵏ(M_{i,0}) = 0 and F_{i,j} Lipschitz; take M_0 := ⋃_i M_{i,0} (null) and the countable family (F_{i,j}).
   - θ > 0 and θ ∈ {1,2,…} on M (step 3).
   - Local integrability: for compact K ⊆ U, K ⊆ V_1 ∪ ⋯ ∪ V_l for some l, hence K ∩ D_j = ∅ for j > l and ∫_{M∩K} θ dHᵏ = Σ_{j≤l} ∫_{M_j∩D_j∩K} θ_j dHᵏ ≤ Σ_{j≤l} ∫_{M_j∩K} θ_j dHᵏ < ∞ (θ is a.e.-strongly measurable on each of the finitely many measurable pieces).

subproblem.natural_proof:
Conventions (fixed for this proof). ℝ^P := Eucl P with standard orthonormal basis e_1,…,e_P. Hᵏ := μHE[k], the normalized k-dimensional Hausdorff measure (a positive constant multiple of μH[k]; it equals Lebesgue measure on a k-dimensional Euclidean space, and μHE[0] = μH[0] is the counting measure). D_k(U) := GeometricCurrentOn U k; D^k(U) := TestFormOn U k (C^∞ k-forms on ℝ^P with compact tsupport contained in U). I(k,P) := the strictly increasing maps {1,…,k} → {1,…,P}; for I ∈ I(k,P), e_I := (e_{I(1)},…,e_{I(k)}) and dx^I is the constant k-covector with dx^I(e_J) = δ_{IJ} (J ∈ I(k,P)); every k-covector is α = Σ_I α(e_I) dx^I. |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α = (Σ_I α(e_I)²)^{1/2} (the norm used in the definition of mass), and ‖ω‖ := sup_x |ω(x)| for a form ω. For a k-vector w (an element of NVector = the dual of the k-covectors) put w^I := w(dx^I) and |w|_* := (Σ_I (w^I)²)^{1/2}; then w(α) = Σ_I α(e_I) w^I, so |w(α)| ≤ |α| |w|_* (Cauchy–Schwarz). M_W(X) := X.massOn W, M(X) := X.mass = M_U(X), spt X := X.support, X_j ⇀ X := WeaklyConvergesOn, ∂ := boundary. τ(M,θ,ξ)(ω) := tauAction = ∫_M θ ⟨ω,ξ⟩ dHᵏ with ⟨ω,ξ⟩(x) := ξ(x)(ω(x)); "i.m." := IsIntegerMultiplicity; "X⌞A" denotes a current S with IsRestriction X A S; W ⊂⊂ U := CompactlyContainedOpen W U. B_r(x), B̄_r(x) denote open and closed balls.

Source: (P6) of the parent proof ("Restrictions converging weakly"), which justifies the printed uses of "4.5(1) and a selection argument as in 6.7(2) of Ch. 2" in Remark 8.3(1), in (1) and in (8) of the printed proof of 8.2; copied and filled in.

Facts used.
(F1) If tsupport ω ⊆ W′ then |Y(ω)| ≤ ‖ω‖ M_{W′}(Y) (if ‖ω‖ > 0, ±ω/‖ω‖ is admissible).
(F2) Lower semicontinuity of mass (Simon 2.14; SimonGMT `WeaklyConvergesOn.massOn_le_liminf`): if Y_j ⇀ Y then M_{W′}(Y) ≤ liminf_j M_{W′}(Y_j) for every W′.
(F3) `iwl_restriction_theory`: (R0) a current with a measure representation has M_{W′} < ∞ for all W′ ⊂⊂ U; (R1) restrictions are unique; (R2) a current Y with locally finite mass has a mass measure μ_Y (IsMassMeasure), restrictions Y⌞B to all Borel B, and M_{W′}(S) = μ_Y(W′ ∩ B) for every restriction S of Y to B and every open W′ ⊆ U. By (R1) we may (and do) compute all restrictions of Y through one fixed representation (μ_Y, v_Y) as in (R2); then (Y⌞B)(ω) = ∫_B v_Y(ω) dμ_Y is countably additive in B, and Y⌞ℝ^P = Y.

Proof.
1. Let C := sup_j M_W(X_j) < ∞. For s ∈ ℝ put W_s := {x ∈ W : φ(x) < s}; it is open because W ⊆ U is open and φ is continuous on U. Put F_j(s) := M_{W_s}(X_j) ∈ [0, C]; F_j is nondecreasing in s (`GeometricCurrentOn.massOn_mono`).
2. (Helly selection.) By a diagonal argument over the countable set ℚ there is a strictly increasing ψ : ℕ → ℕ such that F_{ψ(j)}(q) converges, to F(q) ∈ [0, C] say, for every q ∈ ℚ; F is nondecreasing on ℚ. Put F⁻(s) := sup_{q<s} F(q) ≤ F⁺(s) := inf_{q>s} F(q) and E := {s ∈ ℝ : F⁻(s) < F⁺(s)}. The open intervals (F⁻(s), F⁺(s)), s ∈ E, are pairwise disjoint (monotonicity) subintervals of [0, C], each containing a rational number, so E is countable.
3. Fix s ∉ E, restrictions R_j of X_{ψ(j)} to A_s := {x ∈ U : φ(x) < s} and a restriction R of X to A_s. These hypotheses provide measure representations of X_{ψ(j)} and of X, so by (F3)(R0) all X_{ψ(j)} and X have locally finite mass in U; by (R2) they have mass measures μ_j := μ_{X_{ψ(j)}}, μ := μ_X and fixed representations as in (F3), and by (R1) R_j = X_{ψ(j)}⌞A_s, R = X⌞A_s. Taking B = ℝ^P in the mass identity, M_{W′}(X_{ψ(j)}) = μ_j(W′) for every open W′ ⊆ U; in particular F_{ψ(j)}(t) = μ_j(W_t) for all t. By (F2), μ(W) = M_W(X) ≤ liminf_j M_W(X_j) ≤ C < ∞.
4. (A cutoff adapted to s.) Fix ω ∈ D^k(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ W, and η > 0. The set K_ω := tsupport ω is a compact subset of U and φ is continuous there, so there is a smooth function φ_η on ℝ^P with |φ_η − φ| < η/4 on K_ω (e.g. mollify a continuous extension of φ|_{K_ω} given by Tietze's theorem). Let κ ∈ C^∞(ℝ) with 0 ≤ κ ≤ 1, κ = 1 on (−∞, s − 3η/4], κ = 0 on [s − η/4, ∞), and χ := κ∘φ_η. Then χω ∈ D^k(U), tsupport(χω) ⊆ K_ω ⊆ W, and on K_ω: χ = 1 where φ ≤ s − η, and χ = 0 where φ ≥ s.
5. (Error estimate.) Let Y ∈ {X_{ψ(j)} : j ∈ ℕ} ∪ {X}. By additivity of restrictions, Y(χω) = (Y⌞A_s)(χω) + (Y⌞(ℝ^P ∖ A_s))(χω), and the second term vanishes since χω = 0 on K_ω ∩ {φ ≥ s} (and ω = 0 off U ∩ K_ω). Hence
   (Y⌞A_s)(ω) − Y(χω) = (Y⌞A_s)((1 − χ)ω) = (Y⌞B_η)((1 − χ)ω), where B_η := {x ∈ U : s − η < φ(x) < s},
   because (1 − χ)ω vanishes on K_ω ∩ {φ ≤ s − η}. By (F1) with W′ := W and the mass identity (F3)(R2):
   |(Y⌞A_s)(ω) − Y(χω)| ≤ ‖(1 − χ)ω‖ M_W(Y⌞B_η) ≤ ‖ω‖ μ_Y(W ∩ B_η).
   For Y = X_{ψ(j)}: W ∩ B_η ⊆ W_s ∖ W_{s−η}, so μ_j(W ∩ B_η) ≤ μ_j(W_s) − μ_j(W_{s−η}) = F_{ψ(j)}(s) − F_{ψ(j)}(s − η) ≤ F_{ψ(j)}(q_2) − F_{ψ(j)}(q_1) for all rationals q_1 < s − η and q_2 > s (monotonicity). For Y = X: μ(W ∩ B_η) → 0 as η ↓ 0, because these sets decrease to ∅ and μ(W) < ∞.
6. (Conclusion of (A).) Let ε > 0. Since s ∉ E, there are rationals q_1 < s < q_2 with F(q_2) − F(q_1) < ε; choose η > 0 with s − η > q_1 and μ(W ∩ B_η) < ε. By step 5,
   |R_j(ω) − R(ω)| ≤ ‖ω‖(F_{ψ(j)}(q_2) − F_{ψ(j)}(q_1)) + |X_{ψ(j)}(χω) − X(χω)| + ‖ω‖ ε.
   As j → ∞, the first term tends to ‖ω‖(F(q_2) − F(q_1)) < ‖ω‖ε (step 2) and the second tends to 0 because X_j ⇀ X and χω is a fixed test form. Hence limsup_j |R_j(ω) − R(ω)| ≤ 2ε‖ω‖ for every ε > 0, i.e. R_j(ω) → R(ω). This proves (A).
7. (Proof of (B).) Suppose {x ∈ U : φ(x) ≤ s} ⊆ K with K compact and K ⊆ W. Choose ζ ∈ C_c^∞(W) with 0 ≤ ζ ≤ 1 and ζ = 1 on a neighbourhood of K. For any ω ∈ D^k(U), the form (1 − ζ)ω vanishes on A_s ⊆ K, so (Y⌞A_s)((1 − ζ)ω) = ∫_{A_s} (1 − ζ) v_Y(ω) dμ_Y = 0 for each Y as above. Therefore R_j(ω) = R_j(ζω) → R(ζω) = R(ω) by (A), since tsupport(ζω) ⊆ tsupport ζ ⊆ W. So R_j ⇀ R. ∎
proof_key_steps: F_j(s) := M_{W∩{φ<s}}(X_j) is nondecreasing and bounded; Helly selection on ℚ gives ψ, and the jump set E of the limit is countable.
By iwl_restriction_theory the currents have mass measures and R_j, R are the canonical restrictions; F_{ψ(j)}(s) = μ_j(W ∩ {φ<s}).
With a smooth cutoff χ = κ∘φ_η: |Y⌞{φ<s}(ω) − Y(χω)| ≤ ‖ω‖ μ_Y(W ∩ {s−η<φ<s}).
Bound this by increments of F for X_{ψ(j)} and by continuity of μ_X for X; X_j(χω) → X(χω); conclude (A) at continuity points.
(B): multiply by a cutoff ζ = 1 near K.

For a k-vector w (an element of NVector = the dual of the k-covectors) put w^I := w(dx^I) and |w|_* := (Σ_I (w^I)²)^{1/2}; then w(α) = Σ_I α(e_I) w^I, so |w(α)| ≤ |α| |w|_* (Cauchy–Schwarz). M_W(X) := X.massOn W, M(X) := X.mass = M_U(X), spt X := X.support, X_j ⇀ X := WeaklyConvergesOn, ∂ := boundary. τ(M,θ,ξ)(ω) := tauAction = ∫_M θ ⟨ω,ξ⟩ dHᵏ with ⟨ω,ξ⟩(x) := ξ(x)(ω(x)); "i.m." := IsIntegerMultiplicity; "X⌞A" denotes a current S with IsRestriction X A S; W ⊂⊂ U := CompactlyContainedOpen W U. Source: Step 2 of the parent proof, i.e. Simon Remark 3.12 (p. 149: the codimension-0 case "is a direct consequence of Remark 2.35 and the Compactness Theorem for BV functions (§2.6 of Ch. 2)"), with 2.35 specialized to integer multiplicity currents. Book n = m + 1 = P. (Only integrality of the T_j themselves is needed, not of ∂T_j; this is how the result is also used in Step 11(iv) of the parent proof.)

Notation. n := m + 1, ℝⁿ = Eucl n with standard basis e = (e_1,…,e_n); E := simpleNVector e = e_1∧⋯∧e_n; dx := dx^{(1,…,n)}, the n-covector with dx(e) = 1. Hⁿ = μHE[n] is Lebesgue measure Lⁿ on ℝⁿ.

1. (Top-degree forms.) Λⁿ(ℝⁿ)* is one-dimensional: every n-covector is α = α(e)·dx, and |α| = |α(e)| (I(n,n) has one element). So every ω ∈ D^n(U) is ω = a·dx with a := ω(·)(e) ∈ C_c^∞(U) and ‖ω‖ = sup|a|. For (n−1)-forms, the increasing (n−1)-tuples are I_i := (1,…,î,…,n), i = 1,…,n; write ω = Σ_i ω_i dx^{(i)} with dx^{(i)} := dx^{I_i}; then |ω|² = Σ_i ω_i², and dω = Σ_i (−1)^{i−1} (D_iω_i) dx.
2. (Densities of the T_j.) Write T_j = τ(M_j,θ_j,ξ_j) (i.m.). For Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M_j, ξ_j(x) = ±simpleNVector τ with τ an orthonormal n-frame of ℝⁿ, and simpleNVector τ = det[τ]·E with det[τ] = ±1 (alternating multilinearity; τ = e·[τ] with [τ] orthogonal). Hence ξ_j = σ_j E a.e. on M_j with σ_j := ξ_j(dx) ∈ {±1} measurable. Put β_j := 1_{M_j} θ_j σ_j: integer valued, measurable, and locally Lⁿ-integrable in U (|β_j| = 1_{M_j}θ_j is integrable on compact subsets of U). Then for ω = a dx: T_j(ω) = ∫_{M_j} θ_j ξ_j(a(x) dx) dLⁿ = ∫_U a β_j dLⁿ.
3. (Masses; Remark 2.35 in the i.m. case.) For open W ⊆ U:
   (i) ∫_W |β_j| dLⁿ ≤ M_W(T_j): given a compact K ⊆ W and ε > 0, by Lusin's theorem and mollification there is a ∈ C_c^∞(W) with |a| ≤ 1 and ∫_W |a − sign(β_j)1_K| |β_j| dLⁿ < ε; then T_j(a dx) ≥ ∫_K |β_j| − ε; let ε → 0 and K ↑ W.
   (ii) M_W(∂T_j) = |Dβ_j|(W) := sup{∫ β_j div g dLⁿ : g ∈ C_c^∞(W;ℝⁿ), |g| ≤ 1}: for ω = Σ_iω_i dx^{(i)} ∈ D^{n−1}(U) with tsupport ⊆ W, ∂T_j(ω) = T_j(dω) = ∫ β_j Σ_i(−1)^{i−1}D_iω_i dLⁿ = ∫ β_j div g dLⁿ with g_i := (−1)^{i−1}ω_i, and |ω| = |g| pointwise (step 1); ω ↦ g is a bijection between admissible forms and admissible fields (Simon Ch. 2, 2.4 allows smooth g as well).
   Hence for every W ⊂⊂ U: sup_j (∫_W|β_j| dLⁿ + |Dβ_j|(W)) ≤ sup_j (M_W(T_j) + M_W(∂T_j)) < ∞ by hypothesis; in particular β_j ∈ BV_loc(U).
4. (BV compactness.) By the Compactness Theorem for BV functions (Simon Ch. 2, Theorem 2.6) there are a subsequence (j′) and β ∈ BV_loc(U) with β_{j′} → β in L¹_loc(U). Choosing an exhaustion W_1 ⊂⊂ W_2 ⊂⊂ ⋯ of U (e.g. W_l := {x ∈ U : |x| < l, dist(x, ℝⁿ∖U) > 1/l}) and a diagonal subsequence, β_{j′} → β Lⁿ-a.e. on U. At such a point x the sequence of integers β_{j′}(x) converges, hence is eventually constant, so β(x) ∈ ℤ. Fix a Borel representative β : ℝⁿ → ℤ of this limit with β = 0 outside U.
5. (Identification of T.) For ω = a dx ∈ D^n(U), choose l with spt a ⊆ W_l; then T(ω) = lim_{j′} T_{j′}(ω) = lim ∫ a β_{j′} dLⁿ = ∫ a β dLⁿ, since |∫ a(β_{j′} − β)| ≤ sup|a| ∫_{W_l} |β_{j′} − β| → 0.
6. (T is i.m.) Let M := {x ∈ U : β(x) ≠ 0} (Borel), θ := |β| (θ := 1 off M), ξ := sign(β)·E on M (ξ := E off M). Then τ(M,θ,ξ)(a dx) = ∫_M |β| sign(β) a dLⁿ = ∫ a β dLⁿ = T(a dx), and θ ∈ {1,2,…} on M. IsRectifiableTriple U n M θ ξ:
   - M ⊆ U; M is Borel, hence null-measurable;
   - M is countably n-rectifiable: M ⊆ ℝⁿ = range(id), id Lipschitz;
   - θ > 0 on M, and θ is integrable on M ∩ K for compact K ⊆ U (β ∈ L¹_loc(U));
   - ξ is measurable (two values on Borel pieces);
   - orients: let x ∈ M be a Lebesgue point of β, i.e. r^{−n} ∫_{B̄_r(x)} |β(z) − β(x)| dLⁿ(z) → 0 (Lⁿ-a.e. x, by Lebesgue's differentiation theorem; Lⁿ(B̄_r) = ω_n rⁿ). Take τ := e (orthonormal, span τ = ℝⁿ). Apply `iwl_weighted_tangent_locality` to (M, θ) and (M′, θ′) := (ℝⁿ, the constant function c := |β(x)|) at x: M is Borel and ℝⁿ is measurable (so both are Hⁿ-null-measurable); θ(x) = c = θ′(x); choosing ρ > 0 with B̄_ρ(x) ⊆ U, θ is integrable on M ∩ B̄_ρ(x) and the constant c on B̄_ρ(x); and since 1_M|β| = |β| everywhere (β = 0 off M), for every R > 0
     r^{−n} ∫_{B̄_{Rr}(x)} |1_Mθ − c| dLⁿ = r^{−n} ∫_{B̄_{Rr}(x)} ||β| − |β(x)|| dLⁿ ≤ Rⁿ (Rr)^{−n} ∫_{B̄_{Rr}(x)} |β − β(x)| dLⁿ → 0.
     Moreover HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n ℝⁿ c x ℝⁿ holds: dim ℝⁿ = n, and η_{x,r}(ℝⁿ) = ℝⁿ, so ∫_{η_{x,r}(ℝⁿ)} f(y) c dHⁿ(y) = c ∫_{ℝⁿ} f dHⁿ for every r > 0, which is the required limit. Hence HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M θ x (span e), and ξ(x) = ±simpleNVector e.
   Therefore T = τ(M,θ,ξ) is integer multiplicity. ∎

D_k(U) := GeometricCurrentOn U k; D^k(U) := TestFormOn U k (C^∞ k-forms on ℝ^P with compact tsupport contained in U). I(k,P) := the strictly increasing maps {1,…,k} → {1,…,P}; for I ∈ I(k,P), e_I := (e_{I(1)},…,e_{I(k)}) and dx^I is the constant k-covector with dx^I(e_J) = δ_{IJ} (J ∈ I(k,P)); every k-covector is α = Σ_I α(e_I) dx^I. |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α = (Σ_I α(e_I)²)^{1/2} (the norm used in the definition of mass), and ‖ω‖ := sup_x |ω(x)| for a form ω. Conventions (fixed for this proof). ℝ^P := Eucl P with standard orthonormal basis e_1,…,e_P. Hᵏ := μHE[k], the normalized k-dimensional Hausdorff measure (a positive constant multiple of μH[k]; it equals Lebesgue measure on a k-dimensional Euclidean space, and μHE[0] = μH[0] is the counting measure). D_k(U) := GeometricCurrentOn U k; D^k(U) := TestFormOn U k (C^∞ k-forms on ℝ^P with compact tsupport contained in U). I(k,P) := the strictly increasing maps {1,…,k} → {1,…,P}; for I ∈ I(k,P), e_I := (e_{I(1)},…,e_{I(k)}) and dx^I is the constant k-covector with dx^I(e_J) = δ_{IJ} (J ∈ I(k,P)); every k-covector is α = Σ_I α(e_I) dx^I. |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α = (Σ_I α(e_I)²)^{1/2} (the norm used in the definition of mass), and ‖ω‖ := sup_x |ω(x)| for a form ω. For a k-vector w (an element of NVector = the dual of the k-covectors) put w^I := w(dx^I) and |w|_* := (Σ_I (w^I)²)^{1/2}; then w(α) = Σ_I α(e_I) w^I, so |w(α)| ≤ |α| |w|_* (Cauchy–Schwarz). M_W(X) := X.massOn W, M(X) := X.mass = M_U(X), spt X := X.support, X_j ⇀ X := WeaklyConvergesOn, ∂ := boundary. τ(M,θ,ξ)(ω) := tauAction = ∫_M θ ⟨ω,ξ⟩ dHᵏ with ⟨ω,ξ⟩(x) := ξ(x)(ω(x)); "i.m." := IsIntegerMultiplicity; "X⌞A" denotes a current S with IsRestriction X A S; W ⊂⊂ U := CompactlyContainedOpen W U. B_r(x), B̄_r(x) denote open and closed balls.

subproblem.title: Integrality of weak limits of 0-dimensional integer multiplicity currents
subproblem.statement: Let U ⊆ ℝ^P be open and X_j, X ∈ D_0(U) with every X_j integer multiplicity, sup_j M_W(X_j) < ∞ for every open W ⊂⊂ U, and X_j ⇀ X. Then X is integer multiplicity.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (U : Set (Eucl P)), IsOpen U → ∀ (Xj : ℕ → GeometricCurrentOn U 0) (X : GeometricCurrentOn U 0), (∀ j, IsIntegerMultiplicity (Xj j)) → (∀ W, CompactlyContainedOpen W U → (⨆ j, (Xj j).massOn W) < ∞) → WeaklyConvergesOn Xj X → IsIntegerMultiplicity X
subproblem.natural_proof:
Conventions (fixed for this proof). ℝ^P := Eucl P with standard orthonormal basis e_1,…,e_P. Hᵏ := μHE[k], the normalized k-dimensional Hausdorff measure (a positive constant multiple of μH[k]; it equals Lebesgue measure on a k-dimensional Euclidean space, and μHE[0] = μH[0] is the counting measure). D_k(U) := GeometricCurrentOn U k; D^k(U) := TestFormOn U k (C^∞ k-forms on ℝ^P with compact tsupport contained in U). I(k,P) := the strictly increasing maps {1,…,k} → {1,…,P}; for I ∈ I(k,P), e_I := (e_{I(1)},…,e_{I(k)}) and dx^I is the constant k-covector with dx^I(e_J) = δ_{IJ} (J ∈ I(k,P)); every k-covector is α = Σ_I α(e_I) dx^I. |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α = (Σ_I α(e_I)²)^{1/2} (the norm used in the definition of mass), and ‖ω‖ := sup_x |ω(x)| for a form ω. For a k-vector w (an element of NVector = the dual of the k-covectors) put w^I := w(dx^I) and |w|_* := (Σ_I (w^I)²)^{1/2}; then w(α) = Σ_I α(e_I) w^I, so |w(α)| ≤ |α| |w|_* (Cauchy–Schwarz). M_W(X) := X.massOn W, M(X) := X.mass = M_U(X), spt X := X.support, X_j ⇀ X := WeaklyConvergesOn, ∂ := boundary. τ(M,θ,ξ)(ω) := tauAction = ∫_M θ ⟨ω,ξ⟩ dHᵏ with ⟨ω,ξ⟩(x) := ξ(x)(ω(x)); "i.m." := IsIntegerMultiplicity; "X⌞A" denotes a current S with IsRestriction X A S; W ⊂⊂ U := CompactlyContainedOpen W U. B_r(x), B̄_r(x) denote open and closed balls.

Facts used (with proofs).
(F1) If tsupport ω ⊆ W then |Z(ω)| ≤ ‖ω‖ M_W(Z): if ‖ω‖ = 0 then ω = 0; otherwise ±ω/‖ω‖ is admissible for M_W(Z).
(F0) For 0-covectors α (constants), |α| = |α(∅)| (I(0,P) has exactly one element, the empty tuple), so a 0-form ω is identified with the smooth function x ↦ ω(x)(∅), again denoted ω(x), and ‖ω‖ = sup|ω|.

Proof.
1. (Structure of integer multiplicity 0-currents.) Let Z = τ(M,θ,ξ) ∈ D_0(U) be i.m. Here H⁰ = μHE[0] = μH[0] is the counting measure, so H⁰-null sets are empty. Countable 0-rectifiability gives M ⊆ M_0 ∪ ⋃_j F_j(ℝ⁰) with H⁰(M_0) = 0, i.e. M_0 = ∅, and each F_j(ℝ⁰) is a single point (ℝ⁰ is a point): M is countable. For compact K ⊆ U, Σ_{x∈M∩K} θ(x) = ∫_{M∩K} θ dH⁰ < ∞ and θ ≥ 1 on M, so M ∩ K is finite. The only frame τ : Fin 0 → ℝ^P is the empty one; e := simpleNVector τ is the 0-vector α ↦ α(∅). The orients property holds at H⁰-a.e., i.e. every, x ∈ M, so ξ(x) = σ(x) e with σ(x) ∈ {+1,−1}. Hence
   Z(ω) = Σ_{x∈M} c(x) ω(x), c(x) := σ(x)θ(x) ∈ ℤ∖{0},
   the sum being finite for each test function ω (M ∩ tsupport ω is finite).
2. (Mass lower bound.) If W ⊂⊂ U then Σ_{x∈M∩W} |c(x)| ≤ M_W(Z). Indeed M ∩ W ⊆ M ∩ closure(W) is finite; around each x ∈ M ∩ W choose a ball B_s(x) ⊆ W (W is open) with s so small that these balls are pairwise disjoint and contain no other point of the finite set M ∩ closure(W) (and no point of M outside W, since B_s(x) ⊆ W); choose β_x ∈ C_c^∞(B_s(x)) with 0 ≤ β_x ≤ 1, β_x(x) = 1, and put ω := Σ_x σ(x)β_x. Then tsupport ω ⊆ W, |ω| ≤ 1 (disjoint supports, (F0)), and Z(ω) = Σ_{x∈M∩W} c(x)σ(x) = Σ_{x∈M∩W} |c(x)|. In particular #(M ∩ W) ≤ M_W(Z) and |c(x)| ≤ M_W(Z) for x ∈ M ∩ W.
3. (Local representation of X.) Fix x_0 ∈ U and ρ > 0 with B̄_{2ρ}(x_0) ⊆ U; let W := B_ρ(x_0). W is open, its closure B̄_ρ(x_0) is compact and contained in U, so W ⊂⊂ U and C := sup_j M_W(X_j) < ∞ by hypothesis.
4. Write X_j(ω) = Σ_{y∈M_j} c_j(y) ω(y) as in step 1. By step 2, N_j := #(M_j ∩ W) ≤ C and |c_j(y)| ≤ C for y ∈ M_j ∩ W. Passing to a subsequence (j′) we may assume N_{j′} = N is constant; enumerate M_{j′} ∩ W = {y_{j′,1},…,y_{j′,N}}. Passing to further subsequences (finitely many times) we may assume c_{j′}(y_{j′,i}) = a_i ∈ ℤ is independent of j′ (finitely many integer values in [−C,C]) and y_{j′,i} → z_i ∈ closure(W) (compactness of closure(W)), i = 1,…,N. The subsequence still converges weakly to X.
5. Let ω ∈ D^0(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ W. Points of M_{j′} outside W do not contribute (ω vanishes off W), so X_{j′}(ω) = Σ_{i=1}^N a_i ω(y_{j′,i}) → Σ_{i=1}^N a_i ω(z_i) by continuity of ω. Hence X(ω) = Σ_i a_i ω(z_i). If z_i ∉ W then z_i ∉ tsupport ω, so ω(z_i) = 0. Therefore X(ω) = Σ_{z∈F} b(z) ω(z), where b(z) := Σ_{i : z_i = z} a_i ∈ ℤ and F := {z ∈ W : z = z_i for some i, b(z) ≠ 0} (a finite subset of W).
6. (The local model is i.m.) Let Y := τ(F, |b|, sign(b)·e) (θ := |b| on F, := 1 elsewhere; ξ := sign(b)e on F, := 0 elsewhere). The functional ω ↦ Y(ω) = Σ_{z∈F} b(z) ω(z) is linear and sequentially continuous on D^0(U) (uniform convergence of test functions), so Y ∈ D_0(U). IsRectifiableTriple U 0 F |b| (sign(b)e): F ⊆ W ⊆ U; F is finite, hence Borel and H⁰-null-measurable; F is countably 0-rectifiable (a finite union of images of constant maps ℝ⁰ → ℝ^P); |b| > 0 on F; ∫_{F∩K} |b| dH⁰ is a finite sum; ξ is measurable (finitely many values on a finite set); orients at every z ∈ F with τ the empty frame (orthonormal, span τ = {0}, dimension 0) and ξ(z) = ±simpleNVector τ: for f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P,ℝ) and r > 0, ∫_{η_{z,r}(F)} f(y)|b|(z + r y) dH⁰(y) = Σ_{w∈F} f((w − z)/r)|b(w)|, and for w ≠ z we have |w − z|/r → ∞, so f((w − z)/r) = 0 for small r; thus the integral tends to f(0)|b(z)| = |b(z)| ∫_{{0}} f dH⁰ (H⁰({0}) = 1). Finally τ(F,|b|,sign(b)e)(ω) = Σ_{z∈F} |b(z)| sign(b(z)) ω(z) = Y(ω). So Y is i.m. (|b| ∈ {1,2,…} on F).
7. (Globalization.) By steps 5 and 6, for every x_0 ∈ U there are an open V := W = B_ρ(x_0) with x_0 ∈ V ⊆ U and an i.m. Y ∈ D_0(U) with X(ω) = Y(ω) whenever tsupport ω ⊆ V. By `iwl_im_patching` (with k = 0), X is integer multiplicity. ∎
proof_key_steps: An integer multiplicity 0-current is a locally finite sum Σ c(x)δ_x with c(x) ∈ ℤ∖{0}.
Testing with bump functions shows that the mass on W bounds the number of points in W and their coefficients.
On a ball W ⊂⊂ U, pass to subsequences with a fixed number of points, constant coefficients and convergent positions.
X agrees on forms supported in W with a finite integer Dirac sum, which is integer multiplicity (tangent space {0} at isolated points).
iwl_im_patching globalizes.
